cards.title: Right to Education (RTE Act): Free, compulsory schooling (Ages 6-14)
facts: Article 21A of the Indian Constitution makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right.
Under the RTE Act 2009, schools cannot deny admission, charge capitation fees, or expel kids aged 6-14.
do: Know that every child in India aged 6 to 14 has the legal constitutional right to attend school
Under Section 12(1)(c), private unassisted schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for disadvantaged children
Physical punishment, mental harassment, and screening interviews of children are strictly illegal
dont: Never believe that children from poor families have no legal right to go to school
Never tolerate corporal punishment (beating, canning) in classrooms

myths.statement: Private schools can legally beat students with sticks for not doing homework.
myths.truth: Corporal punishment is strictly illegal under Section 17 of the RTE Act and punishable by law.

quiz.q: Under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution, education is a fundamental right for which age group?
options: Children between the ages of 6 and 14 years
quiz.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment guarantees free, compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.

situations: In a neighborhood at {at}, a 10-year-old child is forced to work in a garage instead of going to school.
scenario.question: What legal constitutional right protects this child?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: The Right to Education (RTE) Act guarantees free, compulsory schooling for ages 6 to 14
Corporal punishment and denying school admission are illegal offenses under Indian law
rubric.note: Affirms legal ban on child deprivation.
rubric.keys: illegal to deny schooling|no child labor|punishable

rubric.point: Report child educational deprivation to local education officers or Childline 1098

dangerous: say schooling is only for rich kids

cards.title: Child Labour Prohibition Act: Why it is illegal and how to report
facts: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act bans employment of children under 14 in all occupations.
Employing adolescents (aged 14-18) in hazardous occupations (mines, chemical factories, fireworks) is a serious crime.
do: Recognize that employing children under 14 in roadside dhabas, tea stalls, or homes is illegal
Understand that child labour deprives young people of their childhood, health, and constitutional education
Report child labour confidentially by calling Childline 1098 or using the PENCiL portal (pencil.gov.in)
dont: Never employ child domestic helpers at home or patronize businesses that exploit young kids
Never ignore young children working in brick kilns, fireworks factories, or hotels

myths.statement: Hiring a 12-year-old child to wash dishes at a roadside tea stall is completely legal in India.
myths.truth: Employing any child under 14 years in commercial work is a criminal offense punishable with jail time.

quiz.q: What official government web portal enables citizens to report child labour violations across India?
options: PENCiL Portal (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour)
quiz.explanation: The PENCiL portal integrates central and district task forces to rescue and rehabilitate child labourers.

scenario.question: What is the responsible legal civic response?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that employing children under 14 is a criminal offense under the Child Labour Act
Report the violation confidentially to Child Helpline 1098 or on pencil.gov.in
Advocate that every child belongs in a school classroom, not behind a commercial dishwashing sink

cards.title: Consumer Protection Act: Maximum Retail Price (MRP) and bills
facts: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, charging even 1 rupee above the printed MRP is strictly illegal.
Consumers have the legal right to receive a proper bill/cash memo for every commercial transaction.
do: Always check the printed Maximum Retail Price (MRP) inclusive of all taxes before paying
Demand a tax invoice or cash memo; without a bill, you cannot claim warranty or file consumer court complaints
File consumer complaints against overcharging or defective goods on the National Consumer Helpline (1915)
dont: Never pay 'refrigerator cooling charges' or extra fees above the printed MRP on cold drinks
Never buy goods with scratched off, pasted over, or tampered MRP labels

myths.statement: Shopkeepers have the legal right to charge ₹5 extra for chilled soft drinks because of electricity costs.
myths.truth: The Supreme Court and Consumer Protection Act rule that MRP includes all taxes and refrigeration costs.

quiz.q: What is the toll-free National Consumer Helpline (NCH) number to report overcharging above MRP?
quiz.explanation: Dialing 1915 connects directly to the Department of Consumer Affairs National Consumer Helpline.

rubric.point: Point out the printed MRP: 'The law states you cannot charge above the printed Maximum Retail Price'

rubric.point: Insist on paying only the legal printed MRP of ₹20 and demand a receipt/bill
Report persistent overcharging merchants to the National Consumer Helpline at 1915

cards.title: What is an FIR: First Information Report and Zero FIR
facts: A First Information Report (FIR) is the written document prepared by police upon receiving information of a cognizable crime.
Under Indian law, a 'Zero FIR' can be filed at ANY police station regardless of where the crime occurred.
do: Know that police are legally mandated under Section 154 CrPC to register an FIR for cognizable offenses
A complainant has the legal right to receive a free physical copy of the registered FIR immediately
Read the recorded statement carefully before signing to ensure your words are accurately documented
dont: Never pay money or bribes to register an FIR (FIR registration is completely free by law)
Never sign a blank sheet of paper at a police station

myths.statement: A police station can turn you away and refuse to file an FIR because the crime happened in another town.
myths.truth: Under the 'Zero FIR' ruling, ANY police station must register the complaint and transfer it to the relevant station.

quiz.q: What is a 'Zero FIR' under Indian criminal jurisprudence?
options: An FIR that can be registered at ANY police station irrespective of territorial jurisdiction
quiz.explanation: Zero FIR ensures swift investigation without jurisdictional delays in emergencies.

scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Understand that police must register an FIR for cognizable crimes and provide a free copy
rubric.keys: register fir|free copy of fir|cognizable offense

rubric.point: Know that if outside home jurisdiction, a 'Zero FIR' must be accepted anywhere
Verify that the recorded statement matches your exact verbal account before signing

cards.title: The POCSO Act: Robust legal shield against child abuse
facts: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act 2012 protects all persons below 18 from abuse.
The POCSO law is gender-neutral, protecting both boys and girls with child-friendly court procedures.
do: Know that POCSO treats anyone below 18 years as a child entitled to maximum legal protection
Reporting is mandatory: any adult, doctor, or teacher who knows of abuse must report it or face imprisonment
Special POCSO courts ensure the child does not see the accused during court testimony
dont: Never believe that the law only protects girls; boys are equally protected under POCSO
Never reveal the identity, name, or school of a child victim in media or public chats (punishable offense)

myths.statement: The POCSO Act only applies to protect female children, not male children.
myths.truth: The POCSO Act is 100% gender-neutral; boys, girls, and transgender children receive identical legal protections.

quiz.q: What is the maximum age limit defining a 'child' under the POCSO Act 2012?
options: Any person below 18 years of age
quiz.explanation: POCSO universally defines a child as any individual who has not completed 18 years of age.

situations: Discussing legal safety in civics class at {at}, students ask about how Indian law protects minors.
scenario.question: What key legal facts should {name} share?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: The POCSO Act is a powerful, gender-neutral law protecting all children below 18 years
Mandatory reporting requires adults and institutions to report abuse to police or Childline
The identity and name of a child victim can NEVER be published publicly by law

cards.title: Right to Information (RTI Act): Holding public offices accountable
facts: The Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005 empowers any Indian citizen to question government decisions.
Public Information Officers (PIOs) are legally mandated to reply with certified records within 30 days.
do: File an RTI request online at rtionline.gov.in with a nominal ₹10 fee to inspect public project records
Use RTI to inspect road repair budgets, school mid-day meal funds, or municipal park contracts
Appeal to the Central/State Information Commission if an office fails to reply within 30 days
dont: Never use RTI for private disputes; it applies strictly to public government authorities
Never feel intimidated: RTI is a celebrated democratic transparency tool for all citizens

myths.statement: Only certified journalists and lawyers have the legal right to file RTI applications.
myths.truth: Every single citizen of India has the constitutional right to file an RTI to inspect government records.

quiz.q: Within how many days is a Public Information Officer (PIO) legally required to respond to an RTI request?
options: Within 30 days of receiving the application
quiz.explanation: The RTI Act mandates a strict 30-day timeline (48 hours if concerning life and liberty).

situations: A road outside school at {at} was supposedly repaired last month but broke apart in 3 days.
scenario.question: How can {name} and their family use the RTI Act constructively?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: File an RTI query on rtionline.gov.in to obtain the sanctioned budget, contractor name, and work audit

Use certified government documents to hold local ward engineers accountable

cards.title: Protecting your Aadhaar and personal data: Masked Aadhaar
facts: Your 12-digit Aadhaar number is a unique national identity linked to banking and mobile telecom accounts.
Sharing unmasked Aadhaar photocopies carelessly exposes you to identity impersonation and SIM swap fraud.
do: Download and use 'Masked Aadhaar' (which displays only the last 4 digits: XXXX-XXXX-1234) from myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in
Cross out the photocopy with two parallel lines and write the specific purpose (e.g. 'For SIM activation only')
Lock your Aadhaar biometrics using the official mAadhaar mobile app when not actively visiting verification centers
dont: Never share your 6-digit Aadhaar OTP with anyone claiming to be a verification executive
Never leave photocopies of your Aadhaar card lying around internet cafes

myths.statement: Hotels and cinema halls have the absolute legal right to demand your original unmasked Aadhaar card copy.
myths.truth: UIDAI explicitly clarifies that Masked Aadhaar is legally valid everywhere, and private entities cannot compel unmasked copies.

quiz.q: What is a 'Masked Aadhaar' downloaded from the official UIDAI portal?
options: An official copy where the first 8 digits are hidden as XXXX-XXXX, displaying only the last 4 digits
An Aadhaar with a mask picture
quiz.explanation: Masked Aadhaar protects privacy by concealing the first 8 digits while remaining 100% legally valid.

situations: Checking into a hotel or registering at a coaching institute at {at}, the clerk demands a photocopy of Aadhaar.

Cross the photocopy and clearly write: 'Submitted strictly for [Purpose] only'
rubric.note: Prevents document misuse for other contracts.

rubric.point: Never share the Aadhaar OTP with anyone under any circumstances

cards.title: Juvenile driving laws: Heavy penalties under Section 199A MV Act
facts: Under Section 199A of the amended Motor Vehicles Act, vehicle owners face 3 years imprisonment if a minor drives.
The vehicle's registration is cancelled for 1 year, and the minor cannot get a driving license until age 25.
do: Understand that underage driving carries a ₹25,000 fine on parents and possible juvenile home detention
Wait until age 18 to obtain a permanent driving license (age 16 for gearless 50cc with parental consent)
Use cycles, walking, or public transport until reaching legal licensing age
dont: Never borrow your parents' car or scooter without having a valid driving license
Never give into peer pressure urging you to show off driving skills outside school

myths.statement: If a 15-year-old drives a motorcycle and causes an accident, police cannot touch them because they are a minor.
myths.truth: Under MV Act Section 199A, parents face 3 years jail, ₹25,000 fine, and the minor faces juvenile justice trial.

quiz.q: What is the legal penalty on parents/vehicle owners under Section 199A if a minor is caught driving?
options: Up to ₹25,000 fine, 3 years imprisonment, and cancellation of vehicle registration for 1 year
quiz.explanation: Stringent MV Act amendments hold vehicle owners criminally liable for allowing underage driving.

rubric.point: State that the minor will be barred from getting a driving license until age 25
Take pride in obeying the law and choose safe cycling or walking

cards.title: Right to be heard at school: Student councils and grievance boxes
facts: Article 12 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child guarantees youth the right to express views freely.
School grievance boxes and elected student councils provide structured channels to voice campus concerns.
do: Use your school's student council or anonymous suggestion/grievance box to raise constructive concerns
Advocate for campus improvements: clean drinking water, clean toilets, library books, and sports gear
Present feedback respectfully with facts, practical solutions, and collective student support
dont: Never use grievance boxes to post anonymous personal insults or defamatory rumors about teachers
Never remain silent about unhygienic washrooms or broken safety equipment

myths.statement: Students are children and have zero right to express opinions about school facilities.
myths.truth: Modern educational jurisprudence recognizes students as primary stakeholders with the legal right to be heard.

quiz.q: What international human rights treaty guarantees children the right to express their views on matters affecting them?
options: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC Article 12)
quiz.explanation: UNCRC Article 12 establishes that children's views must be given due weight in all matters affecting them.

cards.title: Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPWD Act 2016): Equal access
facts: The RPWD Act 2016 recognizes 21 disabilities and mandates barrier-free accessibility in all public buildings.
Discrimination against persons with disabilities is punishable with imprisonment under Indian law.
do: Advocate for ramps, braille signage, and accessible washrooms in schools, metro stations, and public parks
Understand that inclusive education is a legal right: no school can deny admission based on disability
Treat disabled peers with equality, dignity, and natural inclusion without pity or condescension
dont: Never park bicycles or store clutter blocking wheelchair ramps or tactile pavings
Never mock, imitate, or use derogatory slurs against people with disabilities

myths.statement: Wheelchair ramps in schools are optional luxury decorations that schools can skip.
myths.truth: Barrier-free accessibility ramps and accessible washrooms are mandatory legal requirements under the RPWD Act.

quiz.q: How many disabilities are officially recognized under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPWD) Act 2016?
quiz.explanation: The 2016 Act expanded recognized disabilities from 7 to 21, including autism, intellectual disability, and locomotor disability.

cards.title: Article 15: No discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
facts: Article 15 of the Indian Constitution strictly prohibits discrimination in access to public shops, wells, and parks.
Equality is a fundamental pillar: every Indian citizen stands equal before the law.
do: Treat every classmate with equal respect regardless of their family background, language, religion, or caste
Ensure public spaces like colony playgrounds, water coolers, and sports fields are open to everyone
Celebrate India's rich cultural diversity as a source of national strength and unity
dont: Never exclude a classmate from games or study groups based on their caste, community, or mother tongue
Never practice or tolerate untouchability or social segregation (punishable under Article 17)

myths.statement: Colony sports grounds can legally ban children of domestic workers from playing on the grass.
myths.truth: Article 15 explicitly forbids discrimination in public places, parks, and wells against any citizen.

quiz.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth?
quiz.explanation: Article 15 is the cornerstone of non-discrimination and fundamental democratic equality in India.

cards.title: Information Technology Act: What is illegal on the internet
facts: The Information Technology (IT) Act 2000 governs digital crimes, data privacy, and online fraud.
Creating fake social media profiles (Section 66D) or hacking accounts (Section 66) carries up to 3 years imprisonment.
do: Know that online actions leave IP address digital trails that law enforcement cyber cells trace easily
Understand that creating fake impersonation profiles or sending offensive abusive messages is a crime
Respect intellectual property: do not distribute pirated software, cracked games, or copyrighted media
dont: Never create fake social media accounts pretending to be your classmates or teachers
Never hack into a friend's email, Instagram, or gaming account 'as a joke'

myths.statement: Creating a fake Instagram account of your school principal to post funny jokes is harmless and legal.
myths.truth: Identity impersonation and transmitting offensive messages are punishable crimes under Sections 66C and 66D of the IT Act.

quiz.q: What law in India penalizes identity theft, hacking, and online financial cheating?
quiz.explanation: The IT Act 2000 provides the comprehensive legal framework for investigating and penalizing cyber offenses.

cards.title: Lost official documents (Aadhaar, marksheet, passport): Online police report
facts: Lost government IDs can be misused by criminals for unauthorized SIM cards or bank loans.
Filing a 'Lost Document Report' online with state police creates a legal shield proving you did not commit subsequent fraud.

Download and print the official digitally signed Lost Report receipt (LDR) with its unique reference number

cards.title: Child marriage is illegal: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act
facts: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), marriage below age 18 for girls and 21 for boys is illegal.
Anyone who performs, conducts, directs, or abets a child marriage faces rigorous imprisonment and non-bailable arrest.
do: Know that child marriage destroys education, health, and childhood, and is strictly prohibited by law
Know that Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPO), police, and Childline 1098 intervene to stop illegal weddings
Report any impending child marriage secretly and confidentially to Childline 1098 or local police 112
dont: Never attend or support a wedding where the bride or groom is a minor child
Never believe that 'family traditions' overrule the statutory criminal law of India

myths.statement: If parents arrange a wedding for a 15-year-old girl with community approval, the law cannot stop it.
myths.truth: Child marriage is a cognizable, non-bailable offense. Police and Child Welfare Committees halt weddings instantly.

quiz.q: What is the statutory legal age of marriage in India under current law?
options: Minimum 18 years for females and 21 years for males
quiz.explanation: Statutory law mandates minimum 18 for women and 21 for men to protect physical and emotional maturity.

cards.title: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA): Free legal aid for all children
facts: Article 39A of the Indian Constitution directs the state to provide free legal aid to ensure equal justice.
Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, ALL children, women, and disadvantaged citizens get 100% free lawyers.

Access free legal assistance through District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA) in every district court
Call the National Legal Services Authority toll-free helpline at 15100 for guidance
dont: Never assume justice is only for the wealthy who can afford expensive private advocates
Never pay fees to a designated Legal Aid panel advocate (their services are fully funded by the state)

cards.title: Child Welfare Committees (CWC) and juvenile justice protections
facts: Every district in India has a statutory Child Welfare Committee (CWC) acting as a judicial bench for children.
The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act ensures children are rehabilitated, not criminalized.
do: Understand that CWCs have the authority of a judicial magistrate to order shelter, medical care, and rehabilitation
Special Juvenile Police Units (SJPU) in every police station operate in plain clothes to keep interactions child-friendly
Any child found lost, abandoned, or subjected to abuse is produced before the CWC for legal protection
dont: Never treat juvenile justice as punitive; the law focuses on care, protection, and social reintegration
Never publish photos or names of children involved in juvenile proceedings

myths.statement: Police can put children into regular adult prison cells alongside adult convicts.
myths.truth: The Juvenile Justice Act strictly prohibits placing children in adult jails; they receive counseling in observation homes.

quiz.q: What statutory district body holds judicial powers to protect children in need of care and rehabilitation?

cards.title: Passenger rights: Rail cancellations, delays and passenger charter
facts: Indian Railways and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) maintain formal passenger charters.
Passengers have statutory rights to ticket refunds, meals during extended delays, and emergency grievance redressal.

Claim full TDR refunds if a train is delayed by more than 3 hours and you choose not to travel

dont: Never travel without a valid ticket or valid government identity proof
Never pay extra unauthorized cash to railway pantry staff above the printed menu price list

myths.truth: RailMadad (139) takes swift disciplinary action against pantry vendors overcharging above approved IRCTC rates.

cards.title: Fundamental Duties (Article 51A): The citizen's moral compass
facts: Rights and duties are two sides of the same coin; democracy cannot survive if citizens demand rights while abandoning duties.
Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists 11 Fundamental Duties expected of every responsible citizen.
do: Abide by the Constitution, respect the National Flag and National Anthem (Article 51A(a))
Protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife (Article 51A(g))
Develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform (Article 51A(h))
dont: Never destroy or vandalize public property (Article 51A(i) mandates abjuring violence and protecting public assets)
Never treat civic responsibility as someone else's job

myths.statement: The Constitution of India only gives citizens free rights and asks for zero duties in return.
myths.truth: Part IVA (Article 51A) establishes 11 Fundamental Duties essential for national harmony and progress.

quiz.q: Which Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(h) encourages students to question superstitions and explore science?
options: Duty to develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform
quiz.explanation: Developing a 'scientific temper' is a unique, celebrated constitutional duty in the Indian Constitution.

scenario.question: What constitutional wisdom should {name} embody?
